acceptance.criterion_verbatim: JUDGMENT criterion (judgment="true", no invocation minted at cut): the MFA code seal key, HKDF-derived from the JWT private key and deliberately NOT changed by this face -- whether the rotation runbook should also bound it, or should instead bump the v1 label at rotation time.
acceptance.invocation: NOT GRADED HERE BY INSTRUCTION. Evidence assembled for the adjudicator from src/jwt.ts, src/mfa.ts and the deployed bytes.
acceptance.output_evidence: EVIDENCE ONLY -- THIS LANE RECORDS NO VERDICT. (1) THE MECHANISM: getMfaCodeSealKey derives an AES-256-GCM key by HKDF from the JWT private key with the label 'opal-mfa-code-seal-v1', and caches it in cachedMfaSealKey with NO time component. That cache is UNCHANGED by this face, as instructed. (2) THE CONSEQUENCE THIS FACE CREATES, which is NEW and is why it is raised rather than merely inherited: the private key it derives from now refreshes on a bounded window and this derived value does not, so a container living across a TTL boundary holds a seal key derived from a private key it no longer holds. (3) THERE IS NO FUNCTIONAL REGRESSION: seal and unseal within one container still use the same key, and across containers this already diverged before the change. (4) WHAT IS WEAKENED is the invalidation intent the source itself records at the v1 note -- 'changing it invalidates every sealed code in flight, which is the correct behaviour for a key rotation'. After a rotation a long-lived container keeps sealing and unsealing with the OLD derived key even once its private key has refreshed, so that invalidation is less reliable than the note assumes. (5) FAILURE STAYS GRACEFUL EITHER WAY: unsealCode returns null on a wrong key and mfa.ts's callers mint a REPLACEMENT code rather than sending nothing, and verification uses hashCode against the stored row and is untouched -- so the observable effect is that resend-idempotency lapses during the window, not that MFA breaks. (6) THE TWO CANDIDATE REMEDIES, offered without a recommendation: bound this cache too, or bump the v1 label as a deliberate step in the rotation runbook. The consequence is now recorded in a docstring on the function itself so the next reader meets it at the file.

mutant.description: The claim this face stands on is that the signer's key read is now BOUNDED and still returns exactly ONE key -- the CURRENT one. The reading that would make that true on the surface and false in substance is a read that hands the signer the PREVIOUS slot: it would still be bounded, still return a single string, and still pass every shape-level assertion, while letting the signer mint tokens under a retired key. That is the exact failure S10E-AC2 calls a FAIL rather than a bonus.
mutant.expected: With getCurrentKey mutated to destructure previous instead of current, the assertion 'THE SIGNER NEVER RECEIVES previous' must FAIL, and the value-identity assertions must fail with it. If the suite stayed green the control would be certifying nothing.
mutant.observed: 3 passed, 6 FAILED, rc=1 -- and the failing set includes 'THE SIGNER NEVER RECEIVES previous', 'bare PEM returns the key', 'a CHANGED key is picked up after expiry', 'per-secret-id cache: private read returns the PRIVATE key' and 'envelope -> returns CURRENT'. Notably the two CACHE-MECHANICS assertions (hit inside the window, expiry past it) still PASSED under the mutant, which is the point: a timing-shaped test cannot see a wrong-VALUE defect, and only the identity assertions caught it. Restored: 9 of 9, rc=0.
